newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua port strike ends as pay dispute settled.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua port strike ends as pay dispute settled.

text.p: A strike at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua was ended nearly 24 hours ahead of schedule after port operators and dockworkers settled a dispute over pay, union officials said.
"It's been resolved," said the director of the dockworkers' union. "We're going back to work at 1300."
Portworkers at Paranagua went on strike at midday Wednesday in support of dockworkers' demand for a 21 percent pay increase and were originally scheduled to continue until midday Saturday.

The port authority was not immediately available to comment on the end of the stoppage, but a spokeswoman earlier said that normal loading and unloading would resume the moment the strike was called off.
"The export terminal (which handles grains) is ready to start up at a moment's notice," she said.
The port operators' union SINDOP said it had agreed to pay the dockworkers the wage rise until the end of the month and they were due to embark on collective wage negotiations.
"They will have 21 percent until March 31 1997," said SINDOP director Silvio Gori. He added that it was still to be decided whether the wage rise should be made retroactive.
The dockworkers had agreed to cutting the size of work crews and to working 6-hour shifts from April onwards, he said.
